english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^{2}-2x$ and let $g:\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(y)=\dfrac{y^{6}-1}{|y+1|}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}g\big(f(x)\big)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^{2}-2x$ द्वारा तथा $g:\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(y)=\dfrac{y^{6}-1}{|y+1|}$ द्वारा परिभाषित हैं। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}g\big(f(x)\big)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: But $f(x)+1=(x-1)^{2}>0$ for $x\neq1$: $f(x)\to-1$ from the right only
solution_full: The last factor is $1$ for $y>-1$ and $-1$ for $y<-1$. Hence $\displaystyle\lim_{y\to-1^{+}}g(y)=(-2)(3)=-6$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{y\to-1^{-}}g(y)=6$: $g$ has no limit at $-1$, and $g(-1)$ is not defined.
The tempting substitution 'inner limit $-1$, then the limit of $g$ at $-1$' therefore suggests that the limit does not exist. It must be refined by the side from which $f(x)$ approaches $-1$.
$f(x)+1=x^{2}-2x+1=(x-1)^{2}>0$ for $x\neq1$. So as $x\to1$ (from either side), $f(x)\to-1$ through values greater than $-1$, and never equals $-1$.
originality_note: New: the outer function has a jump at -1 (no two-sided limit, no value), but the inner quadratic reaches -1 only at its vertex and approaches it from one side, so the composite limit exists and is the one-sided limit (way 5). Closest known: lim |x - 1|/(x - 1) style one-sided limits. Different because: the side is decided by the inner function (a perfect square), not by the direction of x.
blueprint_concepts: Limits of composite functions and the substitution pitfall

concept_use.Limits of composite functions: lim g(f(x)) is computed through the inner limit f(x) -> -1 and the outer one-sided limit of g.
concept_use.Limits of composite functions and the su: lim_{y->-1} g(y) does not exist, so plain substitution fails; f(x) + 1 = (x-1)^2 > 0 makes only the right-hand limit -6 relevant.
